value.body: A pharma QC analyst tests raw materials, in-process samples and finished medicines in a quality-control lab so they meet set standards. Pharmaceutical and API manufacturers and contract testing labs hire them. A day involves running instruments, following test procedures, recording results and documenting under GMP rules.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc / M.Sc Chemistry or B.Pharm / M.Pharm

items.label: Common instruments
items.value: HPLC, GC, UV-Vis, dissolution testers, Karl Fischer

items.label: Students in B.Pharm
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Ministry of Education (Table 11, all modes)

items.label: Students in M.Pharm
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Ministry of Education (Table 11, all modes)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join as trainee chemists or QC officers through walk-in drives, campus placement or referrals at pharma plants. An M.Sc or hands-on HPLC exposure helps with selection.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Good documentation practice (GDP) and data integrity

value.title: At a glance
items: Most jobs are at plants in industrial clusters, often in shifts.
Common next roles: senior QC analyst, QA officer, analytical method development.
Regulatory audits make careful documentation a central part of the job.

competition.note: B.Sc (all subjects) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
